body_html:
#edu407 Yes the point is let's be more than responsive let's be proactive and and lets think on our history before acting. I often see this with Ellis Island lessons. My son's school does a huge immigrant day and everyone dresses up and goes through Ellis Island. What does this say to handful of minority children who wouldn't have been allowed through?

I see Ellis Island lessons fall flat in cities in New Haven where students role play and complete a quiz while knowing their ancestors came on entirely different ships or knowing that they really weren't welcome in the country now given immigrant status.

The way we can reinforce bias in our classrooms can always come from the best of intentions, and now I wish this class wasn't online so we could all share Latkas and conversation, for critical race theory is so much more than holiday celebrations.
